fullPassage: Warning: Fake News Alert! While scrolling through her social media one day, Gina was astonished when she saw the news headline, “The Heundeulbawi in Seoraksan National Park Has Fallen.” Gina immediately shared the shocking story with her close friends. Later, during the morning news on TV, a reporter standing next to the undamaged Heundeulbawi said, “Today’s Internet stories of the Heundeulbawi being damaged were fake.” Gina was embarrassed by the fact that she had spread the fake news. It reminded her of another incident of fake news that had happened a while ago. The news that a famous athlete had died became the number one issue online, but it turned out to be fake. It had been made by content creators who sought people’s attention. They produced provocative false stories to make money by raising the number of views of their posts. At that time, Gina criticized those who had made and spread fake news because it had hurt the athlete and confused people. This time, however, Gina herself had accidentally contributed to the spread of fake news. The Impact of Fake News on Society Unfortunately, becoming an accidental distributor of fake news like Gina is not unusual. Fake news is a deliberate attempt to manipulate people by spreading inaccurate information. It is made by certain groups with the intention of attracting people’s attention, making profits, or gaining political benefits. It can confuse people, disturb society, and even seriously harm the public as well as all individuals involved. It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency. For example, after an earthquake measuring 6.5 struck Ambon, Indonesia, in September 2019, thousands of residents did not return to their homes and were still in shelters for two weeks. This was because of fake news stories on social media that another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike. One of those messages said, “It’s up to you if you want to believe me or not, but apparently Ambon is going to sink in the next few days.” Many displaced people were so anxious about aftershocks that the government had to announce that the information was fake. The Reasons for the Viral Spread of Fake News Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories. A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that fake news spreads online 6 times faster than real news on average. One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like new and provocative things. When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want to share the stimulating news with others. By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information. Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly. It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it. Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true. In this process, people easily fall into the trap of “confirmation bias.” That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn’t support them. During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates. Ways to Spot and Avoid Fake News With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you? First, read beyond the provocative headlines. They can be so stimulating to get more clicks that you may click on them accidentally. So don’t just read the headlines, but read the text carefully. Second, don’t read the news at face value. Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news. You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read. Third, examine your biases. Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment. Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well. Finally, check the credibility of the source. You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story. You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid. In the digital age, it might be impossible to avoid or eliminate all false information that spreads online. However, if you have the ability to view information critically and objectively, you will be able to reduce the damage that fake news can cause. Don’t forget! Anyone can be the next person producing or spreading fake news!

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ raise → raising: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동사원형이 아니라 동명사(-ing)를 쓰므로 raising
det.analysis:
① had spread: 'Gina was embarrassed by the fact that she had spread the fake news'는 'Gina가 가짜 뉴스를 퍼뜨렸다는 사실에 창피했다'예요. 창피함을 느낀 것보다 '퍼뜨린' 일이 더 먼저라, 한 시제 앞선 과거완료 had spread가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② who: 'content creators who sought people's attention'은 '사람들의 관심을 끌려 한 콘텐츠 제작자들'이에요. 뒤에 동사(sought)가 바로 오고 그 주어 역할을 하니 주격 관계대명사 who가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ raise → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'to make money by raise the number of views'는 '조회 수를 늘림으로써 돈을 벌기 위해'라는 뜻이 되어야 해요. 전치사 by(~함으로써) 다음에는 동사를 그대로 못 쓰고 동명사(-ing)로 바꿔야 해요. 그래서 raise가 아니라 raising으로 고쳐야 맞아요. ❌ raise는 틀림 ←정답

④ criticized: 'At that time, Gina criticized those who ~'는 '그때 Gina는 ~한 사람들을 비판했다'예요. 과거의 일이라 과거형 criticized가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 전치사(by, of, in 등) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing): by raising = ~을 늘림으로써

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② was still → were still: 주어 thousands of residents가 복수이므로 복수 동사 were
det.analysis:
① did not return: 'thousands of residents did not return to their homes'는 '수천 명의 주민이 집으로 돌아가지 못했다'예요. 과거의 사실이라 과거형 did not return이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② was still → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'thousands of residents ~ were still in shelters for two weeks'는 '수천 명의 주민이 2주 동안 여전히 대피소에 있었다'예요. 진짜 주어는 'thousands of residents(수천 명의 주민)'로 복수예요. 복수 주어에는 was가 아니라 were를 써야 하니 was still은 틀려요. were still로 고쳐야 맞아요. ❌ was still은 틀림 ←정답

③ followed: 'another earthquake followed by a tsunami'는 '쓰나미가 뒤따르는 또 다른 지진'이에요. 지진 뒤에 쓰나미가 따라오는 것이라, 앞 명사 earthquake를 꾸미는 과거분사 followed(뒤따르게 된)가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ spreads: 'Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster'는 '소셜 미디어의 가짜 뉴스는 훨씬 더 멀리, 더 빠르게 퍼진다'예요. Fake news는 하나의 덩어리(단수)로 취급하므로 단수 동사 spreads가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: thousands of + 복수명사 = 복수 주어 → 복수 동사(were)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① feeling → feel: 주어 people의 정동사가 필요하고, 뒤의 want와 짝을 이루는 병렬이므로 feel
det.analysis:
① feeling → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'people not only feeling that it is surprising, but they also want to share'는 '사람들은 그것이 놀랍다고 느낄 뿐만 아니라, 그것을 나누고 싶어 한다'라는 뜻이 되어야 해요. 'not only A but also B(A뿐만 아니라 B도)' 구조에서 A와 B는 형태를 맞춰야 해요. 뒤가 want(정동사)이니 앞도 정동사 feel이어야 문장이 완성돼요. feeling(분사)으로 쓰면 주어 people의 동사가 없어져 문장이 안 돼요. 그래서 feel로 고쳐야 맞아요. ❌ feeling은 틀림 ←정답

② gain: 'they can gain attention'은 '그들은 관심을 얻을 수 있다'예요. 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형이 오니 gain이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ to think: 'people ~ tend to think simply and effortlessly'는 '사람들은 단순하고 힘 안 들이게 생각하는 경향이 있다'예요. 'tend to + 동사원형(~하는 경향이 있다)' 구조라 to think가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ examining: 'instead of critically examining it'은 '그것을 비판적으로 따져 보는 대신에'예요. 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 쓰니 examining이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: not only A but (also) B = A와 B의 형태를 맞춘다(병렬): feel ↔ want

When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is ②<u>surprising</u>, but they also want to share the ③<u>stimulating</u> news with others.  By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information.  Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think ④<u>carefully</u> and effortlessly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ carefully → simply: 사람들이 '깊이 따지지 않고 단순하게' 생각한다는 흐름이라 simply
det.analysis:
① farther: 'Fake news ~ spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories'는 '가짜 뉴스는 진짜 이야기보다 훨씬 더 멀리, 더 빠르게 퍼진다'예요. 뒤에 '6배 빠르다'는 연구가 이어지니 '더 멀리(farther)'가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② surprising: 'people ~ feel that it is surprising'은 '사람들은 그것이 놀랍다고 느낀다'예요. 새롭고 자극적인 정보에 대한 반응이라 '놀라운(surprising)'이 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ stimulating: 'they also want to share the stimulating news'는 '그들은 그 자극적인 뉴스도 나누고 싶어 한다'예요. 앞서 사람들이 자극적인 것을 좋아한다고 했으니 '자극적인(stimulating)'이 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ carefully → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly'로 '사람들은 일상에서 단순하고 힘 안 들이게 생각하는 경향이 있다'예요. 바로 뒤에 '증거도 없이 믿고, 비판적으로 따지지 않는다'는 내용이 이어져요. 즉 사람들은 '대충(simply)' 생각한다는 뜻이라, '신중하게(carefully)'는 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 뒤에 '증거 없이 믿는다'가 이어짐 → 생각을 '단순하게(simply)' 함, '신중하게(carefully)'는 반대

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② contradicts → fits: 사람들은 자기 '편견에 맞는(fits)' 정보를 믿는다는 확증 편향의 흐름이라 fits
det.analysis:
① proof: 'believe new information without any proof'는 '아무 증거 없이 새 정보를 믿는다'예요. 비판적으로 따지지 않고 믿는다는 뜻이라 '증거(proof)'가 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② contradicts → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences'로 '사람들은 자신의 편견이나 경험에 맞는 정보를 믿는 경향이 있다'예요. 이 글은 사람들이 자기 생각을 확인해 주는 정보만 받아들이는 '확증 편향'을 설명하고 있어요. 그러니 편견에 '맞는(fits)' 정보를 믿는다고 해야 맞아요. '반대되는(contradicts)'은 정반대 뜻이라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

③ selectively: 'they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs'는 '그들은 자기 신념을 확인해 주는 방식으로 뉴스를 골라서 받아들인다'예요. 입맛에 맞는 것만 고른다는 뜻이라 '선택적으로(selectively)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절

④ blindly: 'people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way'는 '사람들은 지지하는 후보를 긍정적으로 그리는 뉴스를 맹목적으로 믿는 경향이 있다'예요. 따져 보지 않고 믿는다는 뜻이라 '맹목적으로(blindly)'가 맞아요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 확증 편향 = 자기 편견에 '맞는(fits)' 정보만 믿음, '반대되는(contradicts)'은 반대

det.korean: ③ simply and effortlessly(단순하고 힘 안 들이게): 사람들이 깊이 따지지 않고 대충 생각한다는 흐름

❌ ① slowly and carefully(천천히 그리고 신중하게): 신중히 따진다는 뜻이라, 대충 믿는다는 뒤 내용과 반대예요.

❌ ② logically and rationally(논리적으로 그리고 이성적으로): 이성적으로 판단한다는 뜻이라 흐름과 안 맞아요.

✅ ③ simply and effortlessly(단순하고 힘 안 들이게): 증거 없이 대충 믿는다는 뒤 내용과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ deeply and objectively(깊고 객관적으로): 깊이 파고든다는 뜻이라, 대충 생각한다는 흐름과 반대예요.
det.tip: 뒤 문장 '증거 없이 믿고 비판적으로 안 따진다' → 생각을 '단순하고 힘 안 들이게' 함

det.korean: ① critically and objectively(비판적이고 객관적으로): 글 전체가 강조한 '비판적 사고'와 이어지는 결론
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'if you have the ability to view information ___, you will be able to reduce the damage that fake news can cause'(정보를 ___ 볼 수 있는 능력이 있다면, 가짜 뉴스가 초래할 수 있는 피해를 줄일 수 있다). 앞에서 '액면 그대로 믿지 말고, 비판적 사고로 질문·분석·평가하라'고 했어요. 즉 정보를 '비판적이고 객관적으로' 보라는 뜻이에요.

✅ ① critically and objectively(비판적이고 객관적으로): 글 전체가 강조한 비판적 판단과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② quickly and casually(빠르고 대충): 대충 보라는 뜻이라 글의 조언과 정반대예요.

❌ ③ emotionally and personally(감정적이고 개인적으로): 편견을 버리라는 글의 취지와 반대예요.

❌ ④ passively and blindly(수동적이고 맹목적으로): 맹목적으로 믿지 말라는 글과 정반대예요.
det.tip: 글의 핵심 조언 = 정보를 '비판적이고 객관적으로(critically and objectively)' 보라

questions.passage: ” Many displaced people were so anxious about aftershocks that the government had to announce that the information was fake.  The Reasons for the Viral Spread of Fake News Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories.  A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that fake news spreads online 6 times faster than real news on average.  One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like new and provocative things.  When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want to share the stimulating news with others.  By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information.  Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly.  It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it.  Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true.  In this process, people easily fall into the trap of “confirmation bias. ” That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn’t support them.  During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.

questions.passage: Warning: Fake News Alert!  While scrolling through her social media one day, Gina was astonished when she saw the news headline, “The Heundeulbawi in Seoraksan National Park Has Fallen. ” Gina immediately shared the shocking story with her close friends.  Later, during the morning news on TV, a reporter standing next to the undamaged Heundeulbawi said, “Today’s Internet stories of the Heundeulbawi being damaged were fake. ” Gina was embarrassed by the fact that she had spread the fake news.  It reminded her of another incident of fake news that had happened a while ago.  The news that a famous athlete had died became the number one issue online, but it turned out to be fake.  It had been made by content creators who sought people’s attention.  They produced provocative false stories to make money by raising the number of views of their posts.  At that time, Gina criticized those who had made and spread fake news because it had hurt the athlete and confused people.  This time, however, Gina herself had accidentally contributed to the spread of fake news.  The Impact of Fake News on Society Unfortunately, becoming an accidental distributor of fake news like Gina is not unusual.  Fake news is a deliberate attempt to manipulate people by spreading inaccurate information.  It is made by certain groups with the intention of attracting people’s attention, making profits, or gaining political benefits.  It can confuse people, disturb society, and even seriously harm the public as well as all individuals involved.  It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency.  For example, after an earthquake measuring 6. 5 struck Ambon, Indonesia, in September 2019, thousands of residents did not return to their homes and were still in shelters for two weeks.  This was because of fake news stories on social media that another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike.  One of those messages said, “It’s up to you if you want to believe me or not, but apparently Ambon is going to sink in the next few days. ” Many displaced people were so anxious about aftershocks that the government had to announce that the information was fake.  The Reasons for the Viral Spread of Fake News Fake news on social media spreads significantly farther and faster than true stories.  A study by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in the US has shown that fake news spreads online 6 times faster than real news on average.  One explanation for this phenomenon is that people like new and provocative things.  When information is astonishing, people not only feel that it is surprising, but they also want to share the stimulating news with others.  By passing it to others on social media, they can gain attention because they are the first to post previously unknown, but possibly false, information.  Also, fake news goes viral because people in their daily lives tend to think simply and effortlessly.  It is more likely for them to believe new information without any proof, instead of critically examining it.  Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true.  In this process, people easily fall into the trap of “confirmation bias. ” That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn’t support them.  During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news describing their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.  Ways to Spot and Avoid Fake News With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you?  First, read beyond the provocative headlines.  They can be so stimulating to get more clicks that you may click on them accidentally.  So don’t just read the headlines, but read the text carefully.  Second, don’t read the news at face value.  Exercise critical thinking skills to judge the news.  You should question, analyze, and evaluate what you read.  Third, examine your biases.  Consider if your own beliefs could affect your judgment.  Ask yourself if you are only reading articles that suit your opinion, and look for articles that oppose your opinion as well.  Finally, check the credibility of the source.  You should examine who wrote the news story and what the intent was behind writing the news story.  You also need to check whether the news story is from a reliable media source and the evidence is valid.  In the digital age, it might be impossible to avoid or eliminate all false information that spreads online.  However, if you have the ability to view information critically and objectively, you will be able to reduce the damage that fake news can cause.  Don’t forget!

빈칸 문장: 'Finally, check ___'(마지막으로, ___을 확인하라). 바로 뒤 문장에서 '누가 그 뉴스 기사를 썼는지, 어떤 의도로 썼는지 살펴야 하고, 믿을 만한 매체에서 나온 것인지 증거가 타당한지 확인하라'고 했어요. 즉 '출처의 신뢰성'을 확인하라는 뜻이에요.

❌ ① the number of comments it received(받은 댓글 수): 댓글 수는 언급되지 않고 신뢰성과도 무관해요.

✅ ② the credibility of the source(출처의 신뢰성): 뒤에 이어지는 '작성자·의도·믿을 만한 매체 확인'과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ how quickly the story spread online(온라인에서 얼마나 빨리 퍼졌는지): 확산 속도는 이 조언의 핵심이 아니에요.

❌ ④ whether the headline sounds exciting(헤드라인이 흥미롭게 들리는지): 오히려 자극적인 헤드라인을 조심하라고 했어요.
det.tip: 뒤 문장 '누가·어떤 의도로 썼는지, 믿을 만한 매체인지' → 확인 대상은 '출처의 신뢰성'

ch: the number of comments it received
how quickly the story spread online

One of those messages said, “It’s up to you if you want to believe me or not, but apparently Ambon is going to sink in the next few days. ” Many displaced people were so anxious about aftershocks that the government had to announce that the information was fake. questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"수천 명의 주민이 그들의 집으로 돌아가지 못했다." (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) did, homes, not, of, residents, return, their, thousands, to 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: thousands of residents did not return to their homes
det.analysis:
'수천 명의 주민'은 'thousands of + 명사'로 나타내요: thousands of residents(수천 명의 주민). thousands처럼 수를 나타내는 말 뒤에는 of를 붙여요.

'돌아가지 못했다'는 과거의 부정이라 'did not + 동사원형'으로 나타내요: did not return(돌아가지 않았다/못했다).

어디로 돌아가지 못했는가 하면 'to their homes(그들의 집으로)'예요. 방향을 나타내는 to를 쓰고, their homes(그들의 집)를 이어요.

순서대로 이으면 thousands / of / residents / did / not / return / to / their / homes.
det.tip: thousands of + 복수명사 = 수천 명의 ~ / 과거 부정 did not + 동사원형(return)

questions.wa: thousands of residents did not return to their homes
accept: thousands of residents did not return to their homes

questions.passage: Moreover, people are inclined to believe information that fits their prejudices or experiences even when not true.  In this process, people easily fall into the trap of “confirmation bias. ” That is, they selectively accept news in a way that only confirms their beliefs and ignore news that doesn’t support them.  During election season, for example, people tend to blindly believe any news ①<u>described</u> their favored candidates in a positive way, while unconsciously believing news that reports something negative about other candidates.  Ways to Spot and Avoid Fake News With so much information on the Internet, how can you make sure that fake news does not mislead you?  First, read beyond the provocative headlines.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: described → describing: 명사 news를 능동으로 꾸미는 현재분사라 describing
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'people tend to blindly believe any news ①<u>described</u> their favored candidates in a positive way'예요. '사람들은 지지하는 후보를 긍정적으로 그리는 어떤 뉴스든 맹목적으로 믿는 경향이 있다'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 밑줄 친 부분은 앞의 명사 'news(뉴스)'를 꾸며 주는 자리예요. 뉴스가 후보를 '그리는(묘사하는)' 것이니, 능동의 뜻을 가진 현재분사(-ing) describing을 써야 해요. 'news describing their favored candidates'는 'their favored candidates를 묘사하는 뉴스'가 돼요.

described(과거분사)로 쓰면 '묘사된 뉴스'라는 수동의 뜻이 되어, 뒤에 목적어 'their favored candidates'가 오는 것과 맞지 않아요. 그래서 describing으로 고쳐야 맞아요.
det.tip: 명사 뒤에서 꾸미며 목적어를 거느림 → 능동의 현재분사(-ing): news describing ~

questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"가짜 뉴스가 비상 상황 동안 퍼지는 것은 매우 흔하다." (13단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) common, during, emergency, fake, for, is, It, news, of, spread, states, to, very 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 13단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency
det.analysis:
'~하는 것은 매우 흔하다'라는 문장이에요. 진짜 주어(가짜 뉴스가 퍼지는 것)가 길어서, 먼저 가짜 주어 It을 내세우고 'It is very common(그것은 매우 흔하다)'으로 시작해요.

무엇이 흔한지 그 진짜 내용은 'for + 의미상 주어 + to + 동사원형'으로 나타내요: for fake news to spread(가짜 뉴스가 퍼지는 것). 여기서 fake news가 spread의 의미상 주어예요.

'비상 상황 동안'은 during states of emergency로 나타내요: during → states → of → emergency.

순서대로 이으면 It / is / very / common / for / fake / news / to / spread / during / states / of / emergency.
det.tip: 가주어 It ~ for A to B = A가 B하는 것은 ~하다 (진짜 주어는 to부정사)

questions.wa: It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency
accept: It is very common for fake news to spread during states of emergency

"당신은 누가 그 뉴스 기사를 썼는지 검토해야 한다."

[ examine / news / should / story / the / who / wrote / You ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: You should examine who wrote the news story
det.analysis:
주어 'You(당신은)'로 시작하고, '~해야 한다'를 뜻하는 조동사 should와 동사원형 examine(검토하다)을 이어요: You should examine.

무엇을 검토하는가 하면 '누가 그 뉴스 기사를 썼는지'예요. '누가 ~했는지'는 간접의문문 'who + 동사'로 나타내요: who wrote(누가 썼는지).

무엇을 썼는가 하면 'the news story(그 뉴스 기사)'예요. 순서는 the → news → story로 놓아요.

순서대로 이으면 You / should / examine / who / wrote / the / news / story.
det.tip: 간접의문문 who + 동사(who wrote) = 누가 ~했는지 / the news story = 그 뉴스 기사

questions.wa: You should examine who wrote the news story
accept: You should examine who wrote the news story

questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"쓰나미가 뒤따르는 또 다른 지진이 막 닥치려 하고 있었다." (10단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, about, another, by, earthquake, followed, strike, to, tsunami, was 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike
det.analysis:
문장의 주어는 'another earthquake(또 다른 지진)'예요. 어떤 지진인지 꾸며 주려고 과거분사 followed를 뒤에 붙여요: another earthquake followed by a tsunami(쓰나미가 뒤따르는 또 다른 지진). 'A followed by B'는 'B가 뒤따르는 A', 즉 'A 다음에 B가 오는'이라는 뜻이에요.

동사는 '막 ~하려 하고 있었다'를 뜻하는 'was about to + 동사원형'으로 나타내요: was about to strike(막 닥치려 하고 있었다). strike는 '(재난 등이) 덮치다'라는 뜻이에요.

순서대로 이으면 another / earthquake / followed / by / a / tsunami / was / about / to / strike.
det.tip: A followed by B = B가 뒤따르는 A / be about to + 동사원형 = 막 ~하려 하다

questions.wa: another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike
accept: another earthquake followed by a tsunami was about to strike
